newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope, on birthday, says wants to live to 100.
newsitem.headline: Pope, on birthday, says wants to live to 100.

text.p: A jovial, healthy-looking Pope John Paul marked his 77th birthday on Sunday saying that although he was approaching his "sunset", he hoped to live to be 100.
The Pontiff was feted by children and other worshippers of a Rome parish at one of his regular Sunday morning visits to churches in the Italian capital.
Addressing the children, who asked him what his birthday promise was, he replied: "To be good."
"I, after 77 years, am closer to (the) sunset (than you are)," he told them. "You are still children."
When the children chanted the Polish birthday refrain "sto lat" he said: "Do you know that 'sto lat' means 'may you live 100 years'? Well then, I've got 23 to go. Let's hope so. Time passes."
The Pope noted that he was born between five and six p.m. in 1920 and was also elected as head of the Roman Catholic Church between five and six p.m. in 1978.
He neglected to mention that it was also between five and six p.m. that he was shot and nearly killed by a Turkish gunman in St Peter's Square on May 13, 1981.
"These are the moments of my life's history. Everyone has a personal history that leads to eternal life," he said.
The Pontiff, who was born on May 18, 1920 in Wadowice, Poland, has suffered a series of health problems in recent years and undergone several operations.
He is also widely believed to be suffering from Parkinson's Disease or a related ailment that causes his left hand to shake.
But he has said he will not retire and appeared in relatively good form at Sunday's outdoor mass in Rome's working class Tiburtina neighbourhood.

Despite calls from his doctors to slow down his busy schedule of foreign travel, this year is proving one of the most hectic for some time for the Pontiff, whose globetrotting has earned him the nickname of the "Pilgrim Pope".
He has visited Sarajevo, the Czech Republic and Lebanon in recent weeks and is due to make an 11-day trip to his homeland in June. More visits are scheduled to Paris in August and Brazil in October.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in a birthday message that the "fruitful apostolic mission of the Holy Father to all corners of the world, such as the recent visits to Sarajevo and Beirut, is...a constant reminder to work for peace, justice and brotherhood between peoples".
President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro also sent a message of best wishes in the name of the Italian people praising the Pope's mission of "truth, liberty and justice".
"May your voice continue to be one of comfort and encouragement for Italy and for the whole world," he said.
